clue.text: Phoney agent with oil scheming to magnify difficulty

indicators.note: scheming suggests plotting and contriving, so the letters of these words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A fake spy with oil interests plots to make a bad situation worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to exaggerate how painful or hard a situation is, which is to magnify its difficulty.

clue.text: Unconventional part special tip had, say

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual form, so these letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd component — a special tip, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: 'had' is the participle form of the verb 'have', used in perfect tenses, an example of the category.

clue.text: Detailed row about fine note in affair

indicators.note: about means going around the other pieces
de-tailed means having its last letter cut off

parts.note: a row is a line of things
A1 (written AI) means first-rate, fine
so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A detailed quarrel over a fine note in a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'thorough' but means LINE loses its tail, leaving LIN, which goes about AISO.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is an illicit romantic relationship, the sort of secret love affair the clue means.

clue.text: Being without principles, work left college stumped

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship
uni is short for university, a college
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A work about an unprincipled being leaves a college baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exploits chances regardless of scruples is a creature lacking moral principles, a being without them.

clue.text: The northern dash from East End to find marine animal

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is clipped to t'

indicators.note: East End Cockney speech drops the initial H, so the H goes

parts.note: to hurtle is to dash at speed

explanation.surface: A northern dash from London's East End to see a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the Cockney part of London, where speakers drop the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea turtles are reptiles that live in the ocean, so this is a marine animal.

clue.text: Plant bachelor neglected creating joy

indicators.note: neglected means left out, so the letter goes from the plant

parts.note: euphorbia is the spurge plant

explanation.surface: A plant neglected by a bachelor still somehow creates joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is intense happiness and elation, a strong feeling of joy.

clue.text: Begin to work with posh female

definitions.meaning: when plans start to come together and succeed they are said to set or jell

explanation.surface: Starting a job alongside a well-to-do woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to take shape successfully and is also the plummy upper-class way of saying girl.

clue.text: Training sprint held up? True if injured

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to sprint is to run

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A sprinter's training is held up — true, if they are injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses RUN to NUR; 'injured' turns TRUE into TURE. 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture is upbringing and education, the training and care given to someone as they develop.

clue.text: Jack twice showing inconsistent principle?

parts.note: double means twice as much
a jack is a flag, as in the Union Jack, and a flag is a standard

explanation.surface: Jack doing everything twice shows a lack of consistent principles.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue order puts 'Jack' first, but in the answer the word for 'twice' comes first. The question mark marks the definition as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule applied differently to different people is an inconsistent principle, which is what this phrase means.

clue.text: Run about briskly in small vehicle

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a camper is a camper van, a vehicle

explanation.surface: Dashing about briskly in a little car.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to scurry or scuttle quickly, as small animals or children do.

clue.text: Less exciting way of working in Italian city

parts.note: paler means more wan and less vivid, less exciting
MO stands for modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A duller working method in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Palermo is the capital of Sicily, a city of Italy.

clue.text: What drug dealers do endlessly? Unpleasant matter

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: dealers push drugs, i.e. sell them

explanation.surface: Drug dealing presented as an endless, unpleasant business.
explanation.definitionFit: Pus is the yellowish fluid from an infection, distasteful matter in a literal sense.

clue.text: Practical method shown by digital supremacy?

definitions.meaning: a rough working guide based on experience rather than theory
read literally, the dominion of a digit, i.e. a finger

explanation.surface: A working technique shown by the dominance of computing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' looks like computing but means of a finger; the question mark flags the wordplay on the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a rough practical guide; read literally it is the dominance of a thumb, a digit.

clue.text: Injury in news to be broadcast about new driver

indicators.note: about means going around the next piece
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner plate, displayed by a new driver

explanation.surface: News of an injury to a new driver is about to be broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the fodder, not the link: the anagram of IN NEWS TO BE goes about L.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a painful strain of the tendons of the outer elbow, a common sporting injury.

clue.text: Dismissal at centre of furore?

parts.note: a cricket dismissal when a batsman fails to make his ground, often a mix-up that causes controversy

explanation.surface: A sacking that sits at the heart of a public row.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is dismissed this way when the stumps are broken before he completes a run; disputed decisions of this kind are classic causes of a furore.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the ways a batsman can be dismissed in cricket, frequently at the centre of argument.

clue.text: Like Strauss, say, new in, seen batting after struggle

indicators.note: after puts the struggle before the rest

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

indicators.note: batting means knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer, seen batting after a struggle, is compared to Strauss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting' turns SEEN into NESE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss was a Vienna-born composer of waltzes, so he is an example of someone from that city.

clue.text: Imagined sequence in a score improvised

indicators.note: improvised means made up on the spot, so these letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: An imagined sequence of music within a score that was improvised.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a postulated or imagined course of events, an envisaged sequence.

clue.text: Natural feeling this month in court

parts.note: inst. (instant) means of this month in old commercial letters

explanation.surface: A natural feeling this month while appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an innate, unlearned impulse, a natural feeling or tendency.

clue.text: Proper time in part of US for law

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a state is one part of the United States
U means upper-class, socially proper

explanation.surface: The right moment within a state of America to pass a law.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper-class, acceptable' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Nit wife's found in white cotton not unknown

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the next piece
not means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: dimity is a sheer white cotton fabric
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Head-lice eggs found in a wife's white cotton, not otherwise known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nit' looks like a louse egg but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Nit is short for nitwit, a stupid person, a fool or idiot.

clue.text: Western state visited by the Queen, an ambivalent figure

indicators.note: visited by means joined by the following piece

parts.note: to state is to declare or aver
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A western US state visited by the Queen, a figure who cannot decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wavers hesitates between choices, an indecisive or ambivalent person.

clue.text: Knight, one with company in house, getting hot drink

parts.note: K is the chess notation for knight
I is the Roman numeral for one
the RSC, the Royal Shakespeare Company, is a resident theatre company in its own playhouse
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A knight and a friend at home with company, getting a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The RSC is the Royal Shakespeare Company, Britain's leading Shakespearean theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a cherry brandy, a spirit drink.

clue.text: Careless guys fix this blocking current inhabitant

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a native is an inhabitant of a place
guy ropes hold a tent in place

explanation.surface: Careless men repair this, obstructing a current resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' looks like 'men' but means tent ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inattentive is failing to pay attention, the same as being careless or heedless.

clue.text: Leading group is conceited rejecting paper

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: vain means conceited
the i is a UK national newspaper

explanation.surface: A leading group is too conceited to accept a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The van is short for vanguard, the leading group of an army or movement.

clue.text: Act illegally in US city in deficit

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, a US city
under means short of a target, in deficit

explanation.surface: Breaking the law in an American city while running a deficit.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder money is to pass criminal proceeds through legitimate channels, an unlawful act.

clue.text: Failure revealed by Druids oddly

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A failure revealed by Druids, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is something that does not work, a flop or failure.

clue.text: Cold area is backed by secret police chief

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's NKVD secret police

explanation.surface: A cold place is endorsed by a secret police chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the vast frozen region of northern Asia, a byword for a cold area.

clue.text: Late drink by ambassador with tipsy lord definitely out?

parts.note: the late means dead
a tot is a small drink
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so these letters are reeled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dead man drinks with an ambassador and a tipsy lord, definitely out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' turns W and LORD into WORLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fast asleep or unconscious, completely out cold.
